description: Parses the HTTP status out of error events (data.log / data.message) and compares success rates across platforms and player versions, to separate server/CDN-side failures (e.g. 504) from player bugs.

panels.description: 1 - errors/starts, excluding business errors, DRM_NOT_SUPPORTED and CONNECTION_ERROR (same definition as the Daily Report).
panels.title: Success rate

panels.description: Green/red line: normal success rate. Dashed line: the same rate if HTTP 5xx (server/CDN side) errors were removed. If the dashed line stays flat at ~100% while the normal line dips, the dips are fully explained by server-side 5xx responses, not by the player.
panels.title: Success rate vs. success rate without HTTP 5xx

panels.description: Totals for the selected range and filters.
panels.title: Totals
HTTP errors (parsed from the error log)

panels.description: HTTP status parsed from the error message ("Response code: NNN", the same text found in data.log).
panels.title: HTTP status codes over time

panels.description: Share of each HTTP status among HTTP errors.
panels.title: HTTP status share

panels.description: HTTP errors of each status divided by sessions (START) in the same bucket. Normalises for traffic so spikes are real, not just more viewers.
panels.title: HTTP error rate by status (per session)

panels.description: 504 errors / sessions per platform. If Android, Apple and Web spike at the same moments, the cause is upstream (CDN/origin), not the Android player. Note: Apple/Web may word 504s differently — check the Error inspection row and adjust the 'HTTP filter' variable.
panels.title: HTTP 504 rate by platform (ignores platform filter)

panels.description: Success excl. 5xx = success rate once server-side 5xx errors are removed.

targets.root_selector: $map(aggregations.g.buckets, function($b) { { "Platform": $b.key, "Sessions": $b.starts.doc_count, "Errors": $b.errors.doc_count, "HTTP 5xx": $b.http_5xx.doc_count, "HTTP 504": $b.http_504.doc_count, "504 rate": $b.rate_504.value, "Error rate": $b.error_rate.value, "Success rate": $b.success_rate.value, "Success excl. 5xx": $b.success_excl_5xx.value, "Load time": $b.p50_load_time.percentile.values."50.0" } })

panels.title: HTTP 504 impact by platform (ignores platform filter)

panels.description: Success rate over time per Letterbox version (top 10 versions by volume). If all versions dip together at the same moments, the drop is not version-specific.
panels.title: Letterbox success rate by version

panels.description: Success rate over time per Pillarbox version (top 10 versions by volume). If all versions dip together at the same moments, the drop is not version-specific.
panels.title: Pillarbox success rate by version

panels.description: 504 errors / sessions per player version. Similar levels across versions (and players) point to a server-side cause.
panels.title: HTTP 504 rate by player & version

panels.description: Per player name / platform / version. Compare 'Success rate' with 'Success excl. 5xx': when the gap is the same for every version, the errors come from the server, not a particular player release.

targets.root_selector: $map(aggregations.g.buckets, function($b) { { "Player": $b.key[0], "Platform": $b.key[1], "Version": $b.key[2], "Sessions": $b.starts.doc_count, "Errors": $b.errors.doc_count, "HTTP 5xx": $b.http_5xx.doc_count, "HTTP 504": $b.http_504.doc_count, "504 rate": $b.rate_504.value, "Error rate": $b.error_rate.value, "Success rate": $b.success_rate.value, "Success excl. 5xx": $b.success_excl_5xx.value, "Load time": $b.p50_load_time.percentile.values."50.0" } })

panels.title: Player versions — errors and HTTP 504 share

panels.description: Error type × message. Use it to find how each platform words HTTP errors.
